title: Suite transport resets came back and one hit an `always` cleanup: a test product leaked on dev while the rerun reported green
summary: Regression of the [2026-10-21 suite transport reset](2026-10-21-suite-transport-reset.md). In the 17:08Z scheduled run, two anchor flows failed on TCP resets from the Cloudflare edge within one minute: `anchor: resource-permission` on its `always` cleanup `DELETE /v1/products/{id}` (14 ms) and `anchor: auth` on a `POST /v1/auth/refresh` (21 ms). `run_suites.sh` reran both, as the 2026-10-21 fix intended, and both passed, so the run read 25/25. The failed cleanup had left product `prd_3L6X…` on dev Anchor; the green rerun created and deleted its own product, so nothing reported the leftover. The routine found it by reading the failed execution's node results and deleted it at 17:15Z. `run_suites.sh` now prints `TRANSPORT-LEAK` for every `always` node that did not complete, and the flow-suite-testing skill says to clean before trusting a rerun.

impact.text: One throwaway product left on dev Anchor for about 5 minutes; two false red flows, both cleared by the automatic rerun. Dev APIs only, no customer impact.

trigger: At 17:10:14Z the `cleanup-product` DELETE of `anchor: resource-permission` to `apidev.tryanchor.dev` (172.64.80.1:443) was reset by the peer before any response byte.
detection: `run_suites.sh` printed `TRANSPORT-RERUN` for both flows at about 17:13:42Z and both reruns passed. The leak itself was found only because the routine read the failed execution's node results by hand (`GET /flows/{id}/executions/{exec}/nodes`: `cleanup-product` failed with input `prd_3L6X…`). Detection of the leak was not good enough: nothing in the script looked at side effects of a failed run (fixed by A2).
resolution: A one-off flow logged in, read the product (200), deleted it (204) and read it again (404) at 17:15:12Z; the flow was deleted after. `run_suites.sh` now reports every `always` node of a transport-failed execution that did not complete, with its method, path and inputs, before the rerun.

events.label: First transport reset; fix = rerun transport failures once
events.detail: [SEV4 suite transport reset](2026-10-21-suite-transport-reset.md). Its lucky list named this exact risk: a reset on a create or cleanup node can leak a resource. Runner replay (A1) and a sweep (A5) stayed open for humans.

whys.problem: A scheduled suite run left a test product on dev Anchor and still reported all flows green

because.text: The `always` cleanup DELETE of `anchor: resource-permission` failed on a TCP reset, so the product it owned was never deleted
because.evidence: Node results of execution `01a169bd…`: `cleanup-product` failed `CONNECTION_FAILED`, `status_codes [0]`, input `prd_3L6X…`; the one-off GET at 17:15Z returned 200

because.text: Zero response bytes 14 ms after start: the request went onto a pooled keep-alive connection the edge had already dropped
because.evidence: `http_calls[0].durations_ms [14]`, `response_bytes [0]`; the refresh POST failed the same way in 21 ms. A new TLS connection to the edge cannot be set up in that time

because.text: Which hop drops the idle connections (home router, ISP, Cloudflare edge) is not known
The dogfood suites still run from a laptop on a residential network, not from a host with an observed network path
because.evidence: Same decision as 2026-10-21 A4 and 2026-10-17 A3, both still open

because.text: Nothing replayed it: Go's transport replays on a dead reused connection only GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/TRACE; the runner adds no retry
because.evidence: net/http `Request.isReplayable`; echopoint-runner `pkg/node/cloud_dial.go` uses `&http.Client{}` for non-Cloud jobs; `engine.Retry` has no production caller (2026-10-21 evidence)

because.text: Why the 2026-10-21 fix did not hold: it fixed how the suite reports a reset, and left the replay policy as an open human action
because.evidence: 2026-10-21 A1 status open, due 2026-11-04; the ledger row went to verified after two runs with no reset

because.text: The runner treats a transport failure before any response as final even for an idempotent DELETE or PUT
Why so bad: the run reported green, so the leak would have stayed unseen
because.evidence: run_suites.sh output: `TRANSPORT-RERUN` then `✓ Flow 7371aec8…: completed`; anchor 25/25

because.text: The rerun creates and deletes its own product, so its success says nothing about what the failed run left
because.evidence: `anchor: resource-permission` creates a new product on every run (`create-product` POST)

because.text: The transport rerun rule assumed a failed run has no side effects and never read its cleanup nodes
because.evidence: run_suites.sh before 2026-10-23: the transport branch only printed the error and reran

because.text: Why so bad: a leaked test resource stays on dev until someone deletes it by hand
because.evidence: The product was still readable (200) 5 minutes after the failure

because.text: Cleanup exists only inside the run: a suite-made product carries no owner mark or expiry an outside process could act on
because.evidence: `anchor: resource-permission` names its product per run; Anchor products have no TTL field

because.text: The suites were designed so each run owns its data, with in-run `always` cleanup as the only removal path
because.evidence: Run notes: throwaway-org pattern; flow-suite-testing 'Cleanup survives failure'

because.text: No sweep removes suite-made Anchor products or orgs that outlive their run
because.evidence: 2026-10-21 A5 open; the 2026-10-21 lucky list predicted this leak

contributing: The runner labels a read reset on an established connection as `transport_errors: connect` and `Could not connect to …`, which reads like a connect failure, not a dead pooled connection.
The ledger moved the 2026-10-21 row to verified after two runs without a reset while its prevention actions were still open, so the recurrence first looked like a new event.

well: The 2026-10-21 rerun rule turned two resets into an automatic, labelled rerun instead of a manual triage.
Node results keep the cleanup's inputs (`create-product.productId`), so the leaked id was one request away.
wrong: A lucky-list item (reset on a cleanup leaks data) became no guard; it happened two days later.
A green rerun was read as a clean run.
lucky: The leaked resource was a product with no members or keys; a leaked throwaway org would also hold a live 15-minute org API key until it expires.
The reset hit the cleanup, which reads back cleanly. On a create POST after the server wrote, the product id would be unknown and no node result would name it.

actions.what: Runner replays once a DELETE or PUT whose connection failed before any response byte (2026-10-21 A1, now with evidence: dead pooled keep-alive connections); count the replay in `http_calls`
`run_suites.sh` prints `TRANSPORT-LEAK <flow> <node> <status> <method> <path> <inputs>` for every `always` node of a transport-failed execution that did not complete, before the rerun
flow-suite-testing skill: before rerunning an interrupted flow, delete what its uncompleted cleanup nodes still own
Decide the suite host (always-on host or Cloud launches); same decision as 2026-10-21 A4
Sweep suite-made Anchor products and throwaway orgs on dev that outlive their run (2026-10-21 A5)
